docs.purpose: Two tick boxes for the terms of service and the privacy policy, each linking out to the document in a browser. Both must be ticked before the button at the bottom becomes usable. Users who came in to find new work continue to a short celebration screen; users who came in to track existing jobs finish setup here and land straight on their board.
docs.data_story: It reads nothing from the database directly. Every value arrives through one contract: `/api/user-profile`. Behind that contract, the data comes from `entitlements` and `user_profiles`, and writes land on `entitlements` and `user_profiles`. It also holds client-side state in `onboardingStore` and `filterStore`, which is the part a server-driven projection has to absorb or justify. It emits **no analytics event**, so nothing it does is currently countable.
docs.under_126: **REBUILD** — it holds Layer-3 state (`onboardingStore` and `filterStore`) and drives writes, so a client decision has to be re-homed on the server before the projection can be honest. It renders through the WIZARD_STEP renderer (declared step index, advance condition, resume key and skip rule), reading by reference: `/api/user-profile`. It owns no component of its own, so its `owns.components[]` is an empty array — a legal answer, written down.

emits: mobile/app/(onboarding)/terms.tsx:111 — logQueryInvalidate only; no track() call in the file

identity.owner: unassigned (no CODEOWNERS file and no owner registry exists in the repo — measured 2026-09-15)

versioning.why: tos_accepted_at is write-once behind a server TOS_IMMUTABLE fence, and the client reads the cached profile first so it does not even attempt a second write.

inputs.why: It reads the already-cached ["user-profile"] entry to decide whether tos_accepted_at is already set, then PATCHes; the ToS and Privacy documents themselves open in the system browser, not in the app.

outputs.why: Path T finishes onboarding here: it PATCHes default_tab + location_mode + onboarding_complete, AWAITS the ["user-profile"] invalidate, and only then replaces the route — without the await AuthGate would read the pre-PATCH profile and bounce the user back into onboarding.
outputs.rollback: none — no local mirror is written before the server confirms (Spec 99 §9.2b); a failure renders "Setup failed. Please try again." and the user stays on the step.

state.why: It reads onboardingStore.selectedPath to pick between the two completion routes and writes filterStore.locationMode on the Path-T branch; both stores are MMKV-persisted.

staleness.why: The only server value it reads is tos_accepted_at out of the 5-minute ["user-profile"] cache — which is exactly why the completion PATCH must await its own invalidate before navigating.

session.why: Reachable only after AuthGate has a Supabase user whose server profile says onboarding_complete is false; PATCH /api/user-profile is an authenticated route.

rls_class.why: The one table in the path is the caller's own user_profiles row — Class A, policies keyed on auth.uid().

checks.why: mobile/__tests__/terms.test.ts pins all five branches of the cache-read guard: skip the PATCH when tos_accepted_at is set, send it when null, send it on a cache miss.

The completion PATCH awaits queryClient.invalidateQueries(["user-profile"]) BEFORE router.replace; without it AuthGate reads the stale onboarding_complete=false profile and bounces the user straight back (the WF2-B C1 finding, named in the file).
A synchronous useRef guard, not the React `disabled` prop, is what blocks the second of two rapid taps — the disabled prop only updates on the next render (terms.tsx:65-69).
Both checkboxes declare min-h-[44px] min-w-[44px] and the CTA declares min-h-[52px] (terms.tsx:33, 180).

errors.why: One inline red "Setup failed. Please try again." under the checkboxes; the user stays on the step because the server PATCH did not commit.

emits.why: ToS acceptance — a compliance-relevant act — emits no analytics event; the only breadcrumb is the DEV-only query_invalidate from logQueryInvalidate.

offers.why: No sponsored placement is rendered: the only slot component in the Expo tree is SponsorSlot, and it returns null unless EXPO_PUBLIC_PARCEL_SPONSORS=1.

metering.why: Nothing here is counted: the Spec 126 §7 usage ledger table does not exist (grep for usage_events in the introspected drizzle schema returns 0 hits), and the only quota-shaped counter, user_profiles.lead_views_count, is incremented solely by POST /api/leads/view, which has no mobile caller.

config.why: The surface consumes no registered logic variable: the only server-side tunable in this path, user_profiles.radius_cap_km, is a per-user admin column, not a logic_variables row.

sharing.why: PATCH /api/user-profile is rendered by every onboarding step, both shells, settings and the filter sheet.

limitations.what: The ToS and Privacy links are Text onPress handlers with no accessibilityRole, so a screen reader does not announce them as links.
limitations.measured: terms.tsx:144-149 and :159-164 — inline <Text onPress> with className only.

limitations.what: Path T writes location_mode: "gps_live" on the user's behalf because it skipped the address step, without telling the user.
limitations.measured: terms.tsx:94-101 PATCHes location_mode gps_live in the completion body; the rationale (a DB CHECK requires a value) is in the comment at :91-93.

notes: This screen is one of two onboarding terminals: Path L/R continue to the animated complete screen, Path T finishes here and replaces straight to the flight board.

programme.why: Onboarding writes `user_profiles` columns both products read; the flow is shared even though its copy is lead-gen-shaped today.
